dedupe_keys.name: ifpri food and fertilizer export restrictions tracker

description: The Food and Fertilizer Export Restrictions Tracker records export bans, licensing and other restrictions that governments place on food and fertilizer trade, with impact indicators such as the share of traded calories affected. It began as the COVID-19 food trade policy tracker in 2020, expanded after the Russia-Ukraine war, and includes a 2007-2008 food price crisis dataset for comparison. It is produced by the International Food Policy Research Institute (IFPRI) on its Food Security Portal, from news reports verified against official government sources, with funding from USAID, the European Union and the UK FCDO. Coverage is global by country and product; monthly commentary at access ran to August 2026, covering fertilizer restrictions linked to the Middle East conflict, with the next update set for 15 October 2026. Data are free as CSV and XLSX files and through the portal API, under the Open Data Commons Attribution License. Caveats: the page's metadata call it an unmaintained legacy tool although its text shows current updates, and coverage depends on reported measures. For simulation it gives dated trade shocks for food and fertilizer supply chain models and for resilience studies of import-dependent countries. It is related to the Global Trade Alert record in this catalogue, a wider tracker of trade interventions.
